Cross-platform parity: **11.7%**  
Status: **in progress**

The mobile tranche is implemented, documented, and source-matched to an installed Android release.

- [Build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:75) now defines exact-model controls, typography parity, authenticated Courses behavior, consent, materials, and atomic Tutor handoff.
- [Execution plan and pseudocode](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430) records the checkpoint and prevents incomplete M3/M4 work from being counted.
- [Evidence baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:70) is synchronized.

Accepted:

- P0 and D1.
- Internal foundations D2a and M1a remain accepted but contribute no independent progress.

Verified:

- Mobile: 110 tests passing, 420 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript check passed.
- Android export: 2,005 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB Hermes bundle.
- Release APK: 100.1 MB, 946 Gradle tasks.
- Final post-fix APK installed and running on the connected Pixel.
- Local authenticated Courses flow passed through protected 19,778-byte material retrieval.
- Installed app correctly surfaces deployed Courses authentication failure and recovery.

Waiting:

- C1/C2 require the requested Luna review. Luna is unavailable in the current agent/model inventory and no local Luna executable exists. Terra-high review was used.
- Deployed Courses returns `503 notorganic_auth_adapter_unavailable`.
- Picture-in-picture obscures current device captures, so they do not establish look parity.

Completion blockers include native attachments and grounding recovery, complete settings, hosted wallet/token checkout, decks/SRS/profile, native Live, full course collaboration/offline conflicts, public sharing, iOS acceptance, desktop/TUI completion, and clean physical visual comparisons.

`vet` was invoked after each logical change but produced no verdict because it cannot reconstruct the large existing dirty-worktree diff (`DiffApplicationError`).

the application is missing all the usage data and tracking for what you are studying and stuff that whole page is not even there. also can the agent even augment its own code in here?

The mobile gap is now partially closed.

- Added a native [Usage & Study Activity page](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:20), reachable from [More](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/more.tsx:21).
- It reports real local lessons, messages, attachments, artifacts, feedback, study topics, models, provider-reported tokens, and reported cost.
- It explicitly does not fabricate mastery. Quiz evidence, goals, SRS, retention, learner confidence, historical usage, and portable cross-platform records still require the shared learner repository.
- New replies now persist normalized provider/model/token usage. Older replies cannot retroactively recover missing token data.

The composer now supports images and documents through [Add images / Add documents](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/Composer.tsx:154), including validation, draft recovery, removal, transcript rendering, and provider-specific OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter payloads. The Impeccable pass kept these controls compact and recoverable.

Verification:

- 123 mobile tests pass, 448 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript passes.
- Android export: 2,010 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB bundle.
- Release build: 946 Gradle tasks.
- Updated APK installed and launched on the connected Pixel.
- On-device verification confirmed the Usage page and attachment menu.
- I did not select a personal device file, so pick → preview → send remains unaccepted.
- Vet remains unverified because it crashes reconstructing the existing dirty worktree.

On self-augmentation:

- Mobile: no. It cannot rewrite its installed application or this repository.
- Normal web: can modify only its sandbox workspace.
- Locally hosted web with a project root and `--allow-local-exec`: can modify the actual checkout.
- TUI/Pi: yes. Its `edit`, `write`, and `bash` tools can change the working directory.
- `auto-improve`: changes policy and evolved-prompt artifacts; it does not automatically rewrite source code.

The host web and TUI mutation paths should gain an explicit preview/diff/confirmation/validation gate before being considered safe product behavior.

I updated the [build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:118), [baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:54), and [execution checkpoint](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430). `/goal` remains active at 11.7% evidence-weighted completion: these additions do not yet satisfy the full M3 learner-data, Live, recovery, iOS, visual-parity, or required Luna-review gates.

You were right: Usage and study tracking were a major parity gap.

The mobile source now includes:

- A native [Usage & study activity page](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:11) showing lessons, messages, attachments, saved items, feedback, studied topics, models, tokens, and provider-reported cost.
- SQLite-backed, restart-safe learner records with legacy migration.
- Serialized persistence at semantic boundaries such as completed messages, feedback, forks, and artifacts—not every streamed token.
- Honest provenance: lesson titles and artifacts count as study evidence, but do not fabricate mastery.

Still missing before genuine web parity: assessed mastery, goals, decks/SRS, Coming Up, historical charts, learner profile, and learner-facing import/export/delete controls.

On self-augmentation:

- Mobile currently cannot change its own code.
- Web can modify a disposable browser sandbox.
- Web can modify the actual project only when explicitly launched with `--host --allow-local-exec --root=...`.
- Pi/TUI may have local tooling, but OpenTUI lacks a proper capability, confirmation, diff, validation, and rollback experience.
- `auto-improve` evolves teaching policy/prompts; it is not source-code self-modification.

I added that distinction and its required safety gates to the [build plan](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:211), [execution program](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:553), and [parity baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:52).

Verification:

- Mobile: 132 tests, 482 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Shared learner contracts: 22 tests, 165 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Android export: 2,031 modules, 36 assets, 5.6 MB Hermes bundle.
- No Android device is currently connected, so this exact build is not installed/device-accepted.
- `vet` did not produce a trustworthy verdict—it previously crashed on the dirty diff and the latest run hung.
- `/goal` remains active at 11.7%; implementation advanced, but no additional full acceptance node has passed yet.

Implemented the missing mobile learning-data workflow and documented its acceptance state.

- Usage & Study Activity now reports real sessions, topics, feedback, attachments, model/token/cost usage, and provenance.
- Added portable JSON export/share, validate-before-merge import, import preview, conflict/size validation, missing-attachment handling, and explicit deletion controls in [usage.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:177).
- SQLite is now authoritative during import/export and native-state reconciliation in [KeatingProvider.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:776).
- Clearing learning data uses a durable journal so an interrupted deletion resumes after restart instead of restoring partial data: [clear-recovery.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/learner-repository/clear-recovery.ts:10).
- Importing metadata for unavailable attachments shows that the file must be reattached instead of inventing an invalid local URI.

Verification:

- Canonical `keating:mobile-check`: passed
- Mobile: 153 tests, 593 assertions
- Strict TypeScript: passed
- Android export: 2,036 modules, 36 assets, 5.7 MB Hermes bundle
- Current debug APK: built successfully, 242.2 MB
- Physical-device acceptance: pending because no ADB device is connected
- Vet: no verdict; bounded runs timed out during analysis
- Evidence-weighted `/goal` progress remains 11.7%

The remaining usage parity includes historical charts, assessed mastery, goals, decks/SRS, confidence and Coming Up behavior.

On code augmentation: mobile cannot augment its own source today. It deliberately receives no local source-write capability. The planned M2 implementation is an authenticated remote workspace with proposed-diff review, explicit approval, validation, snapshots and rollback. Web has disposable sandbox editing and opt-in trusted host writes; OpenTUI’s underlying CLI has edit/improvement commands, but its confirmation and rollback journey remains unverified.

The current plan and completion program are in:

- [Cross-platform parity build plan](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md)
- [Execution and `/goal` pseudocode](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430)
- [Evidence baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:46)

The goal remains active; M1 is not accepted until the exact APK passes offline, force-kill, export/import/share/delete and restart tests on a physical device.

The missing mobile learning surface is now implemented.

- More → Learn & Coming Up now shows goals, assessed topic mastery, retention, confidence, pending assessments, study priorities, decks, and due reviews.
- Usage remains a separate page for sessions, activity, attachments, feedback, and provider-reported token/cost data.
- Tutor goal, quiz, and question cards persist into SQLite before showing success, preserve answers on failure, retry idempotently, and rehydrate after restart.
- Pending open-ended answers no longer inflate mastery.
- Review scheduling matches web’s Again/Hard/Good/Easy behavior.

Key implementation: [learn.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/learn.tsx:14), [review.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/review.tsx:18), [MessageContent.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/MessageContent.tsx:40).

On self-augmentation: the mobile agent cannot currently modify its own code. It only has text-streaming provider transport; it has no native workspace tool loop. The intended implementation is an authenticated remote workspace with visible diffs, confirmation, snapshots, validation, and rollback.

- Web can edit a disposable NodePod snapshot, or a host project only when explicitly launched with local execution enabled.
- Desktop inherits the web mechanism conceptually, but its packaged augmentation journey is not yet accepted.
- CLI/Pi has explicit edit and improvement commands.
- OpenTUI does not yet have the required capability view and confirmed diff/rollback journey.

The current truth is recorded in [cross-platform-parity-build.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:125), [cross-platform-parity-execution.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430), and [cross-platform-parity-baseline.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:52).

Verification:

- Mobile: 179 tests, 753 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Shared learner contracts: 26 tests, 188 assertions, strict typecheck passed.
- Android: 2,043-module/36-asset export passed; debug APK build passed.
- No Android device is connected, so installed restart/look parity remains unverified.
- Terra-high implementation/review was used. Luna is unavailable in the current agent inventory.
- `vet` entered analysis but produced no verdict because its state log is read-only.

`/goal` remains active at 11.7% evidence-weighted acceptance. The implementation advanced substantially, but the documented graph does not award M3 until Luna review and the physical offline/force-kill learner journey pass.
